APEX-SWE

paper.arxiv.2601.08806

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2601.08806v3. Integration/observability task methods and rubric distinctions establish benchmark-construction scope. The sandbox results do not become deployed engineering reliability. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The leaderboard’s binary test success differs from LM-judged engineering-quality rubrics, which are excluded from leaderboard scoring; the paper reports models that score well on rubrics while still failing task tests.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

APEX-SWE uses a persistent ReAct harness with a one-hour timeout; Integration is graded by service-facing pytest tests, Observability by fail-to-pass/pass-to-pass checks, and Pass@1 averages three independent runs.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

APEX-SWE has 100 Integration and 100 Observability held-out tasks authored by engineers with at leastthree years of experience; Integration includes prompt alignment, test validation and a gold solution, while Observability adapts complex real GitHub issue–PR pairs.
